property_scopes.meaning: the owner an oracle property is reported for: root (once, by the root core), core (each core: main and every child), otherwise source (each core's artifacts, '<core>/<artifact>'); the coverage summary owes a result for every such owner the frozen expected sources establish

incomplete_run_outcomes.meaning: on a recording whose frozen expected sources say complete: false, these properties honestly report the listed outcome (a complete capture is not claimed); that outcome is the expected evidence there, and VERIFIED would claim a completeness the frozen run does not have

property_triggers.meaning: the native scenario whose occurrences make a property applicable to an owner. A NOT_APPLICABLE result is accepted only when the owner's own native records (the frozen expected sources, read by the oracle's source profile within the owner's split scope) hold zero occurrences of the trigger; a VERIFIED result must state how many occurrences it establishes and cover the owner's native population. A property without a declared trigger cannot be answered NOT_APPLICABLE for an applicable obligation.

representation_properties.meaning: properties whose REPRESENTATION_DIFFERS outcome is a declared non-semantic difference (equal values spelled differently, such as 1 and 1.0); on any other property that outcome does not establish the obligation

scenarios: oracle items and route-scoped availability claims name a native scenario (CatalogCoverage#occurrences): run:incomplete, run:children, facts:<family>, path:<inventory path>, value:<path>=<text>, block:<type>|media|unknown, records:opaque

concepts.concept: Session identity (native conversation id)
concepts.question: Which native session does every event belong to, and is that id reported by the CLI rather than assigned by Journal?

foundations.representation: caller-supplied non-empty string key
foundations.identity: assigned by the application that stores memory; not reported by the model or provider
foundations.scope: chat-memory conversation; spans many model calls
foundations.absence: blank id rejected by assertion
foundations.differences: Spring AI's conversation id is a memory-store key chosen by the caller; Journal's session id is the native conversation id the CLI itself reports on every record.
foundations.reason: Same meaning (a key that scopes a continuing conversation) but Journal requires the CLI-reported native id, never an application-chosen key.

foundations.representation: string id on an immutable Session value; every SessionEvent carries sessionId
foundations.identity: CreateSessionRequest.id or a random UUID assigned by DefaultSessionService
foundations.scope: one continuous conversation stored in a SessionRepository; ChatMemory deprecated in favor of it
foundations.absence: Session.build() rejects an empty id
foundations.differences: An application-owned conversation log identity rather than a CLI-reported native session id; no notion of a native id that differs from the store's.
foundations.reason: Session log identity is close to Journal's session scope, but its id is application- or UUID-assigned, so Journal keeps the CLI's own id and does not adopt Spring's assignment.

foundations.selector: NewSessionResponse.sessionId; params.sessionId on session/prompt, session/update, session/request_permission
foundations.representation: opaque string SessionId
foundations.identity: issued by the Agent (the CLI) on session/new; reused by session/load and session/resume
foundations.scope: conversation context across prompt turns and reconnects
foundations.absence: required on every session-scoped message
foundations.differences: Same meaning; ACP delivers it on the wire whereas Journal reads it from native records and stores it on every event.
foundations.reason: ACP's agent-issued sessionId has Journal's meaning: the CLI's own id scoping prompts, updates and permission requests.

foundations.representation: string attribute on GenAI spans
foundations.identity: conversation (session, thread) id held by the framework or backend
foundations.scope: per span; conditionally required (iff readily available or provided by the application) on inference, agent and tool spans
foundations.absence: SHOULD NOT be populated when unavailable; a new UUID, trace id or content hash MUST NOT be used as fallback
foundations.differences: Optional per-span attribute; Journal requires session_uid on every event. Neither models resume/continuation linkage.
foundations.reason: Same meaning, including the rule that the id is reported, never fabricated; Journal only raises the requirement level.

foundations.representation: string span attribute (context attribute)
foundations.absence: not specified
foundations.differences: OI does not require the id to be the native CLI conversation id; it is whatever the instrumentation or application sets.
foundations.reason: Journal keeps the meaning but requires the native id reported by the CLI on every event.

foundations.representation: string column on every agent span row
foundations.identity: plugin 0.4.0 sets the Claude Code session id, walking the resume chain to the original id
foundations.scope: every row; there is no session row
foundations.absence: absent attribute becomes an empty string
foundations.differences: Resumed sessions report the original session id rather than the current native id; Journal records the id each record reports and leaves resume linkage unresolved.
foundations.reason: Same meaning; Journal does not rewrite ids through a resume chain and keeps the empty/absent distinction.

foundations.reason: The release common model is one model call (ChatModel.call/stream) with role-typed messages; it has no prompt-turn identity or lifecycle markers. Journal's turn definition stands alone.

foundations.selector: SessionEvent.isTurnStart() (MESSAGE event whose message is a USER message)
foundations.representation: derived boundary over the ordered session event log
foundations.identity: no turn id; a turn is identified only by its starting user-message event id
foundations.scope: turn = user message plus everything until the next user message; a model call inside it is a round
foundations.absence: no submitted/started/completed markers; completion is implied by the next user message
foundations.differences: Derived from message order with no turn id or lifecycle events; Journal uses the CLI-reported turn id and records submission, start and completion separately.
foundations.reason: Spring's turn meaning (one user message through the replies, tool calls and results up to the next user message) matches; Journal keeps native turn ids and explicit start/completion records Spring does not have.

foundations.representation: JSON-RPC request/response pair
foundations.identity: no turn id; only the JSON-RPC request id correlates request and response
foundations.ordering: one active turn per session; updates arrive between request and response
foundations.scope: prompt turn; final when the session/prompt response arrives
foundations.absence: cancellation ends with stopReason cancelled
foundations.differences: No protocol turn identifier and no separate 'started' event; Journal records the CLI's native turn id and its own lifecycle records.
foundations.reason: ACP's turn (session/prompt to the stopReason response) is the reference lifecycle; Journal adds the CLI's native turn id because ACP has none.

No turn identity or submitted/started/completed lifecycle; invoke_agent spans describe an agent invocation, and mapping one turn to one invoke_agent span is an emitter choice (as the Weave plugin does).
No turn id or turn lifecycle; only session.id, user.id, graph.node.* and span kinds (AGENT, CHAIN).

foundations.scope: turn; root closes only at the next prompt, SessionEnd or daemon shutdown
foundations.absence: system-injected input (background-task notification) opens an extra root with no typed prompt
foundations.differences: No submitted/started/completed records; the turn id is synthetic; root duration includes idle time; extra roots for injected input.
foundations.reason: Journal keeps one turn per submission but uses native turn ids where reported and explicit lifecycle activities.

concepts.concept: User submission (user-role message that is a human prompt) and its repeated representations
concepts.question: What submissions occurred, and which records are repeat representations, history or injected context rather than new submissions?

foundations.representation: user-role message with text plus an unordered media list
foundations.ordering: position in the prompt's message list
foundations.scope: one prompt sent to one model call
foundations.absence: text required (non-null) for USER messages
foundations.differences: Any user-role content is a UserMessage; there is no notion of repeated representations, history or injected context.
foundations.reason: Role meaning only: Spring cannot tell a new submission from history replay or user-role injected context, which Journal must distinguish.

foundations.selector: UserMessage parts; SessionEvent of type MESSAGE with isSynthetic()==false
foundations.representation: user-role message with an ordered parts list, wrapped in a session event
foundations.absence: synthetic flag absent means not synthetic
foundations.differences: Distinguishes real input from compaction shadow prompts only; Journal also separates repeat representations and user-role injected context.
foundations.reason: Closer than release: a non-synthetic USER message event is 'real user input' and synthetic compaction prompts are flagged; repeated representations of one submission are still not modeled.

foundations.selector: PromptRequest.prompt (ContentBlock[]); user_message_chunk.content with optional messageId on replay
foundations.representation: ordered ContentBlock array
foundations.identity: optional opaque messageId on chunks; none on the session/prompt request itself
foundations.absence: messageId optional
foundations.differences: ACP has one canonical representation per submission; native CLI files can carry the same submission several times, which Journal must mark as repeats.
foundations.reason: ACP separates the live submission (session/prompt) from replayed history (user_message_chunk), matching Journal's intent; Journal additionally reconciles repeated native representations.

foundations.representation: ordered list of {role, parts[]} messages; structured on events, JSON string on spans
foundations.ordering: MUST be in the order sent to the model
foundations.scope: per inference request; prior history repeats in every request
foundations.absence: opt-in (not captured by default); MAY be filtered or truncated
foundations.differences: Records what the request carried, so earlier submissions, history and injected user-role content repeat; no marker separates a new human submission.
foundations.reason: Journal keeps the role/parts meaning but identifies the submission once and classifies repeats and injected context separately.

foundations.representation: flattened indexed attributes per LLM span; raw request in input.value
foundations.ordering: zero-based message index in request order
foundations.absence: hideable via OPENINFERENCE_HIDE_INPUTS / HIDE_INPUT_MESSAGES
foundations.differences: Same request-carried view as OTel: repeated history and system-injected content are indistinguishable from a new submission.
foundations.reason: Journal needs submission identity, not request contents.

foundations.selector: AgentSpanSchema.input_messages[] (NormalizedMessage role/content) on the root invoke_agent row
foundations.representation: list of {role, content, finish_reason}; content is text or a JSON parts string
foundations.scope: turn root row and first chat row
foundations.absence: attachments, images and files are not captured by the plugin
foundations.differences: Plugin takes the UserPromptSubmit prompt text, so it is a submission rather than request history, but text only and injected input becomes its own root.
foundations.reason: Journal keeps the submission meaning and the exact blocks, including non-text content.

concepts.question: What did each message contain, in native order, with every block's exact native representation retrievable?

foundations.representation: one text string, a tool-call list and a media list (no ordered blocks)
foundations.ordering: lost across kinds; Anthropic text blocks are concatenated and thinking blocks moved into separate Generations
foundations.absence: unsupported block types are dropped (logged)
foundations.differences: No ordered block list and no per-block native data; Journal keeps block_index plus the whole native block.
foundations.reason: Message content meaning only; 2.0.1 stores text, tool calls and media as separate fields, so native block order is not recoverable and Journal cannot use its shape.

foundations.selector: AbstractMessage.getParts() -> List<MessagePart> (TextPart, ReasoningPart, ToolCallPart, ToolResultPart, MediaPart, UnknownPart)
foundations.representation: ordered sealed list of typed parts with a 'type' discriminator (since 2.1.0)
foundations.identity: no part id; optional attributes (e.g. provider item id)
foundations.ordering: native order as produced or supplied; legacy builders fall back to text, tool calls, media
foundations.absence: unknown types become UnknownPart instead of failing
foundations.differences: Typed normalized parts, not exact native blocks; streaming index attributes are stripped after aggregation.
foundations.reason: Adopt the ordered-parts meaning (interleaving preserved, accessors are projections); Journal keeps the native block whole with ACP-style kind and exact vendor type instead of typed Java parts.

foundations.selector: ContentBlock {text, image, audio, resource_link, resource} in agent_message_chunk / agent_thought_chunk / user_message_chunk; tool activity as tool_call updates
foundations.representation: one ContentBlock per chunk notification
foundations.scope: streamed message within a prompt turn
foundations.absence: no block index; reasoning and tool calls are separate update kinds
